Q: How do I get more than 2k characters of an external js code for a bookmarklet? A:

Old question but check out this repo: https://github.com/KLVN/MediasiteDownloader

How it works:

  • Beautified JS code that is reader-friendly

  • GitHub action that minifies this JS code, but keeps it working as a Bookmarklet

  • jsDelivr CDN that grabs the minified script from GitHub (https://www.jsdelivr.com/github)

  • To avoid caching issues after updating the script, the current time will be appended to the request URL. You can also force-purge the cache: https://www.jsdelivr.com/tools/purge

Q: How can I encode the filename parameter of Content-Disposition header in HTTP? A:

I was trying all this stuff today in response to a customer issue:

  • With the exception of Safari configured for Japanese, all browsers our customer tested worked best with filename=text.pdf, where text is a customer value serialized by ASP.NET and IIS in UTF-8 without URL encoding. For some reason, Safari configured for English would accept and properly save a file with a UTF-8 Japanese name but that same browser configured for Japanese would save the file with the UTF-8 characters uninterpreted. All other browsers tested seemed to work best/fine (regardless of language configuration) with the filename UTF-8 encoded without URL encoding.
  • I could not find a single browser implementing RFC 5987 and RFC 8187 at all. I tested with the latest Chrome, Firefox, Internet Explorer 11, and Edge. I tried setting the header with just filename*=utf-8''texturlencoded.pdf, setting it with both filename=text.pdf; filename*=utf-8''texturlencoded.pdf. Not one feature of RFC 5987 or RFC 8187 appeared to be getting processed correctly in any of the above.

Q: Way to create multiline comments in Bash? A:

Use : ' to open and ' to close.

For example:

: '
This is a
very neat comment
in bash
'

Q: What is exact meaning of "kitchen sink" in programming? A:

It is an english word which is basically an approach, i.e., Kitchen Sink is an approach. Its meaning is:

everything that can be conceived of

Q: How to model data to Rust type A:

My immediate gut feeling seeing DataState is that it's doing too much work and representing too many things in one enum, although the overlap between fetch errors and no-data vs stale data don't quite decompose cleanly. I'd recommend sketching a design where DataState is a struct holding separate enums: one to represent a fetch error vs no attempt (no wifi/not yet attempted) vs successful fetch, and another for no/stale/fresh, and see how that feels.
